01 — OVERVIEW

A queue you can join from anywhere

QueueMate is a mobile app that lets people join a queue from their phone instead of standing in one. Customers find a company and take a ticket, companies see their day at a glance, and staff serve people in turn.

I designed the core screens for the customer and company experiences, plus the shared entry flow that sends each person down the right path. The screens shown in this case study are the main screens of the app, not every screen.

Check out the live app →
02 — THE PROBLEM

Waiting shouldn’t mean standing still

At banks, clinics and shops, a physical line ties people to one spot. Step away and you may lose your place. Stay and you lose the time. For the business, the line is hard to see: how many are waiting, who is being served, and how busy the day really is.

1

Remove the physical line

Let customers join a company’s queue from their phone and step away while they wait.

2

Make waiting visible

Show queue position, waiting counts and open status in real time, for customers and companies alike.

3

Keep it simple for everyone

Three very different users, one app. Every screen should answer its user’s question at a glance.

03 — WHO IT’S FOR

One app, three roles

The product serves three audiences with different jobs to do, so the very first decision after the welcome is who you are.

Customer

Finds companies, joins their queue, gets a ticket number and tracks their position live.

Company

Registers the business, sets working hours and a queue window, and manages staff and the day’s queue.

Staff

Logs in to serve customers efficiently with one-tap controls.

04 — DESIGN DECISIONS

What shaped the experience

◐

Roles with their own weight

On role select, Customer is a light card, Company a dark one and Staff the brand green, so each audience spots its path instantly. Settings lets anyone switch role later.

●

Status first

Each company card shows an open badge, waiting count and queue hours up front, so “can I queue here now?” is answered before a single tap.

▢

Calm, scannable cards

Rounded cards, generous spacing and an icon, a short label and one supporting line keep dense information easy to read.

⌂

Familiar navigation

The same four tabs (Home, Profile, Settings, About) appear everywhere, with the active tab as a filled green pill.

♡

Reassuring copy

Tips like “Your spot is saved — feel free to step away while you wait” answer the anxiety of leaving a line.

05 — VISUAL LANGUAGE

Green means go

A confident green carries the brand and signals “open”, “available” and “go”. A deep ink tone adds contrast for the company role, and red appears only on the role switch in these screens.

Queue Green#00A63E · primary, open states
Ink#101828 · text, company role
Mint#F3FCF6 · app surface
Alert Red#E7000B · switch role
06 — KEY SCREENS

The experience, screen by screen

These are the main screens of QueueMate, not all of them. The full app has more screens than shown here.

Welcome & onboarding

  • Floating chips (ticket A001, 5 min, 12 waiting, Open) preview the product’s vocabulary before anyone reads a word.
  • Onboarding explains the customer flow in three short lines: search, get your ticket, track your position.
  • A mini preview of the company list shows what “open” and “closed” look like.

Who are you?

  • One question routes people to the right experience: Customer, Company or Staff.
  • Colour and contrast differentiate the three choices, each with an icon and a one-line promise.
  • Reassurance that the role can be switched anytime in Settings lowers the cost of choosing wrong.

Customer home

  • A personal greeting and a search field put finding a company first.
  • Company cards show category, open status, people waiting and queue hours at a glance.
  • Helpful tips at the bottom explain how waiting works and when joining is allowed.

Company home

  • A status banner confirms the queue is open and counts down to closing time.
  • “Today’s Activity” turns the day into three numbers: waiting, serving and done.
  • Quick actions give one-tap access to the dashboard, queue, staff and settings.

Profile & settings

  • The company profile gathers identity, daily stats, contact email, working hours and queue window in one place.
  • Settings keeps preferences light: notifications, sound effects, dark mode and a role switch.
  • The role switch is the only red element, marking it as the one action that signs you out.

About

  • Four short cards sum up the promise: easy queue management, real-time updates, fast one-tap controls and reliable service.
  • The same card pattern is reused, so even an information screen feels part of the system.

07 — WHAT’S NEXT

Where I’d take it

Test the join flow

Run usability tests on joining a queue and tracking a position to find friction before launch.

Design the staff experience

Give staff a focused serving screen with one-tap next, skip and complete controls.

Improve empty states

New companies see zeros everywhere, so guide them to add the first staff member and share their queue.
